problem: Graph-based navigation treats unexplored frontiers as semantically unknown, and when VLM-predicted frontier semantics are used, wrong predictions get embedded in memory and propagate through dependent inferences; confidence attenuation leaves the erroneous subgraph in place.
motivation: Semantic frontier prediction can speed up exploration, but VLM errors (mirrors, glass) accumulate over long-horizon episodes. A memory that can retract false premises and everything derived from them should keep memory reliable while still exploiting semantic priors.
key_idea: Represent frontier predictions as revisable hypothesis nodes in a dependency DAG, verify them on arrival against actual observations, and on mismatch delete the refuted node together with all its downstream dependents.
insight: Both components matter and reinforce each other: removing the semantic hypothesis module drops GOAT subset SR 72.41 to 67.71, and removing cascade correction drops it to 68.61. Local-delete-only (70.85 SR) and soft decay + revisit penalty (70.17) both fall short of full cascade deletion (72.41), so structural pruning of descendants beats score-based mitigation. Cascade correction matters more with weaker VLMs (refuted share rises from 26.5% to 35.1% with LLaVA-1.5-13B). Caveat: the numbers are self-reported on a 10% subset, and the paper is internally inconsistent in places.
method: Hypothesis graph: nodes split into observed nodes (verified) and hypothesis nodes (VLM semantic distribution, unverified). Navigability edges plus a dependency DAG D with confidence-weighted parent-child edges, restricted to a single parent per node (forest).

Semantic hypothesis module: GPT-4o predicts a room category distribution and expected objects for each frontier from the frontier image and local detected objects within 3 m, adding room-to-object child hypotheses.
Exploration scoring: S = P(goal category) - λd·geodesic distance + λh·entropy, with λd=0.15 and λh=0.10, used to rank frontiers.
Prediction residual test: Δsem = 0.4·category mismatch + 0.3·(1 − CLIP similarity) + 0.3·object Jaccard dissimilarity; refute when > 0.5.
Cascade correction: on refutation, BFS over the DAG removes the node and all transitive descendants from the graph, so the graph can shrink (non-monotonic).
Confirmation: a confirmed hypothesis is promoted to an observed node, with its children re-parented to it and observed-node features updated on revisit.

setting.backbone: GPT-4o (frozen) for hypothesis generation; CLIP for residual; DD-PPO low-level controller
setting.training_data: none (training-free; hyperparameters tuned on a held-out validation split)
setting.action_space: frontier/waypoint selection executed by a DD-PPO controller (forward 0.25 m / turn 10°)

results: On the GOAT-Bench 278-subtask subset HGR reaches 72.41 SR / 56.22 SPL vs 3D-Mem 69.1 / 48.9 (+3.31 SR, +7.32 SPL); on the full validation set 64.14 / 50.1 vs 62.9 / 44.7. A-EQA LLM-Match is 55.9 vs ConceptGraph w/ Frontier 47.2, and EM-EQA is 58.3 vs Multi-Frame 48.1.
limitations: Cascade correction depends on the accuracy of the residual test: false positives prune valid nodes and false negatives let errors persist
Prediction quality is bounded by the VLM (mirrors, glass and spatial relations account for most errors); it adds ~24% wall-clock overhead from extra VLM calls
Main results are on a 10% subset in simulation only, against re-implemented baselines; the single-parent forest simplification and static-scene assumption limit generality
